Kaneki Auth use cases

Who uses one app's auth deployment, what they can do, and which flow diagram shows each step.

  • Updated2026-11-10
  • Better Auth1.7.19
  • Scopeone app's deployment
  • Companionflows · ERD · architecture

What the service does, on one page

Short answer

Each app's Kaneki Auth deployment serves 6 kinds of actor through 23 use cases: 8 account use cases for end users, 7 OAuth use cases for external apps and their APIs, and 8 for admins, machines and a daily job. S1S2S3

8account use cases
7external-app use cases
8admin, machine & job use cases
14sequence diagrams

Who uses the service

ActorWho it isTalks to Kaneki Auth through
End userA person using one of your appsThe sign-in, consent and reset pages in a browser
Client appThe external app (SPA, mobile or server-rendered) that wants the user signed inOIDC redirects and /oauth2/token S4
Resource APIThe app's own API that receives access tokensThe cached JWKS. Introspection only for opaque tokens S5S6
App backend / scriptCode acting for itself, with no userClient credentials or an API key S7S8
AdminYou, the owner, with the admin role in that app's databaseThe admin endpoints S9S10
Daily cronA Vercel cron jobOne custom clean-up route S11

Google and Gmail SMTP are supporting systems, not actors: Kaneki Auth calls them and they never call in first. S12S13

Rules and variations

Rules that apply across use cases

RuleEffectApplies to
Each app has its own deployment and databaseThe same person has separate accounts in app 1 and app 2, and there is no single sign-on between them S2S19All
user.email is uniqueOne account per email per app. Google sign-in with a known email links to that account S20S21UC-01, UC-04, UC-05
Magic link signs up new emailsUnless disableSignUp: true is set, which makes the app invite-only for magic links S22UC-05
PKCE S256 requiredEvery authorization request needs a code_challenge S4UC-09, UC-10
Always send resourceOtherwise the access token is opaque, and UC-14 becomes UC-15 on every call S7UC-10, UC-16
The resource must be registeredAn unknown resource gives invalid_target S3UC-09, UC-16, UC-19
Client credentials are off per clientAn admin must allow the grant and its scopes S7UC-16, UC-18
Email goes through sendMail()Gmail SMTP now (500 a day), Resend later S13S19UC-01, UC-02, UC-05, UC-06
Cron runs at most daily on HobbyClean-up is a once-a-day batch S11UC-23

Not in scope (by decision or for now)

  • Single sign-on across apps: excluded by design, since each app has its own user pool. S2
  • Organizations and teams: the organization plugin is not used. S19
  • Self-service client registration (dynamic registration): kept off. Only admins register clients. S19
  • Two-factor authentication, passkeys, phone sign-in: not chosen. Better Auth has plugins for these if needed later. INFERRED (plugin folders two-factor and phone-number exist in the 1.7.19 package. Passkey was not checked)

Open questions for review

  1. Sign-up policy per app: open sign-up, or invite-only (disableSignUp, admin-created users)? OPEN
  2. First admin: how is the admin role granted in each new app's database? OPEN
  3. UC-08 UI: should end users get a page that lists and revokes their app consents, or is the endpoint enough for now? OPEN
  4. UC-17: are API keys needed in phase 1 at all? OPEN
  5. Account deletion by the user is not listed. Should it be a use case? OPEN
